claim:
Let \(X=(\mathbb R^2,N)\) be the real regular-octagonal Banach plane
\[
N(u,v)=\max\left\{|u|,|v|,\frac{|u|+|v|}{\sqrt2}\right\}.
\]
Let
\[
J(X)=\sup_{x,y\in S_X}\min\{N(x+y),N(x-y)\}.
\]
Then \(J(X)=\sqrt2\), and
\[
\min\{N(x+y),N(x-y)\}=\sqrt2
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
y=\pm Qx,
\]
where \(Q(u,v)=(-v,u)\). Consequently every James-extremizing pair satisfies
\[
N(x+y)=N(x-y)=\sqrt2.
\]
Thus the complete equality set consists exactly of Euclidean quarter-turn pairs.
integrity: The proof exhausts a dihedral fundamental domain and all five upper-half boundary pieces; no finite sampling is used as proof.
scientific_limitations: Specific to the displayed real regular-octagonal norm and the ordinary James constant.
title: Rigidity of James extremizers in the regular octagonal Banach plane
